info.name: u-l10n API
info.description:
HTTP API of **u-l10n**, the in-house localization service. Generated from the route
table in `route/route.go` and the handler code in `route/`; mirrors
`docs/API.md`, with the handlers winning where they disagree.

HTTP only, on `:8080`. Every response is JSON except the export zip and the OTA
304. Timestamps always leave the service as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

## Two auth schemes

- **Humans** authenticate with the portal's Google access token:
  `Authorization: Bearer {{googleToken}}`. Two facts are established in order —
  Google answers WHO (failure is 401, re-authenticating might help), then this
  service's own `users` table answers WHAT (failure is 403, re-authenticating
  never helps). Roles are ordered `viewer < editor < approver < admin`, each
  route states its minimum, and an unknown role satisfies nothing — it fails
  closed. `is_platform_admin` is a separate flag, not a fifth role. The
  `x-yp-role` header the portal also sends is ignored entirely; the portal must
  gate its UI on `GET /api/v1/me`.
- **Scripts and CI** authenticate with `X-Api-Token: {{apiToken}}`. Scopes are
  ordered `read_export < read_write`. Export needs `read_export`; every asset
  route needs `read_write`, including the presigned GET, because the screenshots
  carry customer PII.

Auth is set at the FOLDER level here and inherited: collection auth is `none`,
the Google folders carry bearer auth, Export and Assets carry the `X-Api-Token`
header, and Health and OTA send nothing.

There are no HTTP routes for managing API tokens or creating users — both are
CLI commands (`token`, `user grant`), on purpose.

## Strict inputs

**Unknown query parameters are REJECTED with 400, not ignored** — a client that
misspells `untranslated_in` must be told, not handed an unfiltered page. Every
optional parameter in this collection is therefore present but **disabled**, so
it cannot fire by accident. Unknown JSON body fields are refused the same way
(`DisallowUnknownFields`), the body must be exactly one JSON object, and it is
size-capped: 64 KiB on portal routes, 8 KiB on asset routes. Booleans accept
exactly `true`/`false`; integers must be non-negative, and a present-but-
unparseable value is a 400 rather than a silent default.

## The three-state translation rule

A `(key, locale)` pair has THREE states, not two, and they are different
everywhere they appear — cells, history, branch diffs and merge conflicts:

```json
{"translated": false}                     // no row: UNTRANSLATED, omitted from exports under skip_empty
{"translated": true,  "value": ""}        // a row holding "": DELIBERATELY BLANK, exported as ""
{"translated": true,  "value": "Top up"}  // translated
```

`PUT .../translations/{locale}` with `""` writes a deliberate blank; making a
pair untranslated is `DELETE`, never `null`. Collapsing the two states adds ~430
spurious keys to en-SG or deletes 3,664 intentional blanks from ms-MY.

Translation and key writes take an optimistic-concurrency `base_version`, and a
lost race answers 409 `version_conflict` whose body carries BOTH `mine` and
`theirs` so the portal needs no second round trip.

## Project scoping (route move is PLANNED, not done)

`/projects` and `/projects/{project}/locales*` are project-addressed today.
**Every other route in this collection is NOT project-prefixed yet** — keys,
branches, merge requests, releases, tags, export and OTA all resolve against
project id 1 (YouTrip), hardcoded and marked `TODO(plan-2)` in the handlers and
services. Moving them under an explicit project prefix is planned; treat the
`{{project}}` variable as applying only to the Platform admin folder for now.

## Rate limiting

One in-process token bucket per client IP, shared across `/api/v1` and `/ota/v1`,
running BEFORE authentication because the expensive paths are pre-auth. Over
budget: 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` in whole seconds. Defaults are 300
requests/minute sustained, burst 60. `/healthz` and `/readyz` are exempt by
MOUNTING, not configuration — a kubelet that gets 429 from a liveness check
restarts a healthy pod.

## Error envelope

`{"error": "<machine_code>", "details": "<human message>"}`; `details` is omitted
when empty, and a 500 body is always just `{"error":"internal_error"}` — the
reason goes to the log, not the wire. 400 = the caller sent something wrong,
404 = the thing addressed does not exist, 409 = the caller's view of the world is
out of date (always an expected workflow outcome, never a fault), 500 = a
genuinely unrecognised failure.

## Variables

Set `baseUrl`, `googleToken` and `apiToken` first; the id-shaped variables
(`keyId`, `mrId`, `tagId`, `assetId`, `releaseVersion`, `branchName`,
`userEmail`) are placeholders to fill in as you go.

item.name: Health
item.description: Probe endpoints. No auth and NOT rate-limited: the kubelet presents no credentials, and a probe that can fail for auth or budget reasons is a probe that reports the wrong thing.

request.description:
**No auth. Not rate-limited** (a 429 on a liveness probe would restart a healthy pod).

Reports process liveness and deliberately touches no dependency — it answers "is this process wedged?" and nothing else.

200 `{"status":"ok","service":"u-l10n"}`. There is no error path: a database outage must NOT fail this probe.

**No auth. Not rate-limited.**

Pings the database and reports whether this instance can serve traffic now. Kubernetes removes a failing pod from the Service endpoints but leaves it running — the correct response to an unreachable database.

200 `{"status":"ready","checks":{"database":"ok"}}`.
503 `{"status":"unavailable","checks":{"database":"unreachable"}}` when the ping fails.

item.name: Export
item.description: `X-Api-Token`, minimum scope `read_export`. Auth is inherited from this folder.

query.description: REQUIRED. `json` (Flutter), `xml` (Android) or `strings` (iOS).
Comma-separated locale codes; absent = every active locale. Empty elements and a trailing comma are dropped, not errors.
`include` (default — emit the key with an empty value) or `skip_empty` (omit the key entirely). Anything else is 400.
`lf` (default) or `crlf`. Anything else is 400.

request.description:
**`X-Api-Token`, minimum scope `read_export`** (`read_write` also satisfies it).

Renders the requested format for the requested locales and returns the archive synchronously — the response body IS the zip, there is no job to poll.

200 `Content-Type: application/zip`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="u-l10n-<format>-<UTC timestamp>.zip"`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (the archive reflects mutable state).

**Parameters** — only `format`, `locales`, `empty_mode`, `line_ending` are accepted; anything else is 400 `bad_request` naming the parameter. `format` is REQUIRED.

**`locales` is one comma-separated parameter, not a repeatable one.** The handler reads it with `Query().Get`, so a second `locales=` occurrence is silently ignored rather than merged — send `locales=en-SG,ms-MY`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` (missing/unknown `format`, unknown parameter, unknown locale, export-name collision, bad `empty_mode` or `line_ending`); 500 `export_failed` for anything else. Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

item.name: Assets
item.description: `X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write` on every route — including the presigned GET, because these context screenshots carry customer PII and a token issued only to pull translations has no business reading them. Three-step flow: presign -> the browser POSTs the bytes straight to S3 -> confirm. The image bytes never pass through this service. Auth is inherited from this folder.

request.description:
**`X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write`** — every asset route needs `read_write`, including the presigned GET, because these screenshots carry customer PII.

Validates a declaration and returns a signed multipart/form-data upload target, or the existing asset when these exact bytes are already stored.

200 with either `{"deduplicated":true,"asset":{...}}` (skip the upload) or `{"deduplicated":false,"upload":{"url","fields":{...},"s3_key"}}`. Every field must be POSTed to S3 verbatim — they are signed, and S3 rejects an altered or omitted one. The URL and fields are credentials and are never logged.

Body rules: `content_type` must be `image/png` or `image/jpeg`; `bytes` must be 1..10485760 (10 MiB); `sha256` is the hex digest of the bytes; `filename` is cosmetic and truncated to 200 chars. Bodies on the asset routes are capped at 8 KiB.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` (validation failure, unknown JSON field, oversized body). Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

**`X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write`.**

Records the asset after verifying the object really landed in S3. The body is ONLY the hash on purpose: everything else is read back from the object's own metadata, which S3 enforced against the signed policy, so there is no second client declaration that could disagree with the first.

201 `{"id","sha256","filename","content_type","bytes","uploaded_by","created_at"}`. `uploaded_by` is `token:<name>`.

Errors: 409 `upload_not_found` — no uploaded object for that hash (409 and not 404: the endpoint is fine, the state the client believes in is not); 409 `upload_mismatch` — the object does not match, or does not carry, its declaration; 400 `bad_request`. Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

**`X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write`.**

Issues a short-lived presigned GET for one asset.

200 `{"url":"<presigned GET>"}` with `Cache-Control: no-store` — the URL is a bearer credential for customer PII and must not be cached anywhere.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` when `{id}` is not a positive integer; 404 `not_found` for an unknown asset. Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

**`X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write`.**

Links an existing asset to a key. PUT rather than POST because attaching is idempotent: repeating it with a different note amends the note rather than creating a second link.

204 No Content on success.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` when `{id}` is not a positive integer or `asset_id` is missing/non-positive; 404 `not_found` for an unknown key or asset. Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

**`X-Api-Token`, scope `read_write`.**

Removes the link between a key and an asset. The asset itself survives — the bytes are content-addressed and another key may still reference them.

204 No Content on success.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` when either path id is not a positive integer; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors: 401 `missing_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: X-Api-Token realm="u-l10n"`), 401 `invalid_token` (wrong, revoked and expired are indistinguishable on purpose), 403 `insufficient_scope`, 429 `rate_limited`.

item.name: Identity
item.description: Google access token, minimum role `viewer`. Auth is inherited from this folder.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns the caller's identity and role — `{"email":"a@you.co","role":"editor"}`. This is what the portal must gate its UI on; the `x-yp-role` header the portal also sends is ignored entirely (it describes YouPortal's group model and arrives from the client, which makes it a request, not a fact).

Nothing is queried — the middleware already read the row.

No query parameters: any parameter is 400 `bad_request`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

item.name: Read
item.description: Reading the corpus. Google access token, minimum role `viewer` — seeing the copy that ships in the app is the least a provisioned operator can do, and a translator who cannot read the existing strings cannot write consistent ones. Auth is inherited from this folder.

query.description: View the corpus as this branch sees it; absent = master.
Comma-separated locale codes to include; absent = every active locale. Unknown code is 400.
`flutter`, `android` or `ios`. Anything else is 400.
Only keys carrying this tag name.
Text search over key name/description/values.
Only keys with NO row for this locale (absent, not blank).
Strictly `true` or `false`; anything else is 400.
Non-negative integer, capped at 20000 (400 above that). 0 or absent = no limit applied by the handler.
Non-negative integer.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Bulk fetch behind the key browser. Every parameter is optional, and unknown ones are refused with 400 rather than ignored — a portal that misspells `untranslated_in` must be told, not handed the unfiltered corpus.

200 `{"keys":[...],"total":N,"limit":N,"offset":N,"locales":[...],"branch":null|"name"}`. `total` is the whole matching set, not the page; `branch` is null on master. Each key carries `id`, `name`, `description`, `platforms`, `android_name`/`ios_name` (null = derive from the key name), `status`, `version`, `sort_index`, `tags` (always an array), `values` keyed by locale code with an entry per requested locale, `branch_modified`, timestamps.

Each cell obeys the three-state rule: `{"translated":false}` = untranslated, `{"translated":true,"value":""}` = deliberately blank, otherwise translated. `version` is MASTER's version and is what you send back as `base_version`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an unknown parameter, `limit`/`offset` that is not a non-negative integer, `limit` above **20000**, `include_deleted` that is not exactly `true`/`false`, an unknown `platform`, or an unknown locale code in `locales`/`untranslated_in`; 404 `not_found` for an unknown `branch`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

query.description: Resolve the key as this branch sees it; absent = master.
Comma-separated locale codes; absent = every active locale.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns one key with its values, in the same shape as a row of the browser list.

200 the key object.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` when `{id}` is not a positive integer, or for an unknown query parameter (only `branch` and `locales` are accepted); 404 `not_found` for an unknown key or branch. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

query.description: Restrict the value timeline to one locale.
Default 200, capped at 1000 (400 above that).

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns the key's metadata and value timelines. Both tables are insert-only: a rollback appears as a new forward entry, never as a deletion.

200 `{"key":[...],"translations":[...]}`. Translation entries carry the same three-state `translated`/`value` pair — a null value in history means the pair BECAME untranslated, which is a different event from becoming blank. `branch_id` is null for a change made on master.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an unknown parameter (only `locale` and `limit`), a non-integer/negative `limit`, `limit` above **1000**, or a non-positive `{id}`; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

query.description: `open`, `merged` or `closed`; absent = all. Anything else is 400.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`** — seeing what work is in flight is reading, not writing.

Returns every branch with its delta counts.

200 `{"branches":[...]}`. Each branch carries `id`, `name`, `description`, `status`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `last_edited_at` (null until the first write — this is what invalidates an approval), `merged_at`, `value_changes` / `meta_changes`, `merge_request_id` (null when there is no LIVE request) and `merge_request_status`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an unknown parameter or a `status` outside `open`/`merged`/`closed`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns one branch with its delta counts.

200 the branch object.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an empty name or ANY query parameter (this route accepts none); 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns the branch's diff against master. Every row carries a `conflict` flag computed with the merge's OWN version comparison — a diff that disagreed with the merge would have a reviewer approve a clean-looking change and watch the merge refuse it.

200 `{"branch","status","values":[...],"meta":[...],"conflicts":N}`. Value rows carry both sides in three-state form: `removed` = the branch tombstones the pair (the merge DELETEs master's row rather than blanking it), `master_translated:false` = master has no row at all. `conflicts` counts the flagged rows across both lists.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for any query parameter or an empty name; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

query.description: One of `open`, `approved`, `changes_requested`, `rejected`, `merged`, `closed`; absent = all.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Lists merge requests, newest first.

200 `{"merge_requests":[...]}`. Each carries `id`, `title`, `status`, `branch_id`, `branch`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `approved_by`/`approved_at` (null until approved, and RESET to null when a later branch edit invalidates the approval) and `merged_at`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an unknown parameter or a `status` outside the six known values. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns one request with its branch, timeline and conflicts. The conflicts travel with it deliberately: a review screen that fetched them separately would render "ready to merge" for the moment before the second request answered, and that moment is when somebody clicks.

200 `{"merge_request":{...},"branch":{...},"events":[...],"conflicts":{...}}`. Event `actor` is `"system"` for automatic transitions, such as an approval invalidated by a later branch edit.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for any query parameter or a non-positive `{id}`; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns everything blocking the merge, in all three kinds.

200 `{"values":[...],"metadata":[...],"name_collisions":[...],"unresolved":N,"mergeable":bool}`. Value and metadata conflicts are resolved by choosing a side (`resolution` is `mine`, `master`, or empty while undecided). **Name collisions carry no resolution field** — both sides independently claimed a name and one key has to be renamed; choosing a side cannot fix it, so they are excluded from `unresolved`.

`mergeable` is **ADVISORY**: the merge recomputes all of this inside its own transaction under an advisory lock, and that answer is the one that counts.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for any query parameter or a non-positive `{id}`; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns every tag with its usage count, in one query — the tag manager renders the whole list, and a count per row would be one round trip per row.

200 `{"tags":[{"id","name","colour","key_count","created_at"}]}`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for ANY query parameter (this route accepts none). Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

query.description: Default 50 when absent or 0. Maximum 500 — above that is 400 `bad_request`.
Non-negative integer.

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `viewer`** — knowing what shipped is reading; changing what ships is not.

Returns release history, newest first.

200 `{"releases":[...],"limit","offset"}`. Each release carries `id`, `version`, `source`, `notes`, `merge_request_id` (null for a manual publish or an import — the difference between "somebody approved this" and "somebody pushed it"), `min_app_version` (null = every client eligible), `created_by`, `created_at`, `rolled_back`/`rolled_back_at`/`rolled_back_by`, `locale_count`, `key_count`.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for an unknown parameter, a non-integer or negative `limit`/`offset`, or **`limit` above 500** (`releasesvc.maxListLimit`; note docs/API.md documents the default but not this cap). Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns one release. Releases are addressed by their human-facing VERSION rather than their row id — that is the number in the incident channel when somebody says "roll back 41".

200 the release object.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` when `{version}` is not a positive integer, or for any query parameter; 404 `not_found`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`.**

Returns exactly what a release shipped for one locale, read from the MATERIALISED bundle rather than re-derived from master — the whole point of materialising at merge time is that the answer cannot drift afterwards.

200 `{"version","locale","sha256","key_count","byte_size","strings":{...}}` with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300` — private because it sits behind an identity, and caching it in a shared proxy would serve one operator's authenticated response to another. `sha256` is the same fingerprint that doubles as the OTA ETag.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for a non-positive `{version}`, an empty or unknown `{locale}`, or any query parameter; 404 `not_found` when the release has no bundle for that locale. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token, minimum role `viewer`** — knowing which projects exist is reading, not administering one. Creating or reconfiguring a project needs `is_platform_admin` (see the Platform admin folder).

Returns every live project; archived projects are excluded.

200 `{"projects":[{"id","code","name","status","lokalise_project_id","created_at","updated_at"}]}`. `lokalise_project_id` is OMITTED, not sent as `""`, when the project has no Lokalise source at all.

Errors: 400 `bad_request` for ANY query parameter (this route accepts none). Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

item.name: Write
item.description: Writing the corpus. Google access token, minimum role `editor`, and no higher: writing to a BRANCH is the safe act by construction — nothing reaches an app until a merge, and a merge needs an approver. Auth is inherited from this folder.

query.description: Write to this branch as a copy-on-write delta; absent = write master directly. The branch must be open (409 `branch_not_open` otherwise).

request.description:
**Google token, minimum role `editor`.**

Adds a key. With `?branch=` it is created as a draft on master plus a branch delta the merge promotes — until then it is invisible to every export and every OTA bundle.

201 the created key.

Body rules: `name` required, <= 255 chars, no leading/trailing whitespace, no control characters; `description` <= 2000 chars; `platforms` required and non-empty, each of `flutter`/`android`/`ios`; `android_name`/`ios_name` are optional export-name overrides (null = derive from the key name).

Errors: 400 `bad_request` (validation, unknown JSON field, unknown query parameter — only `branch` is accepted); 409 `name_taken` when an active key already claims the name; 409 `branch_not_open`; 404 `not_found` for an unknown branch. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token + `is_platform_admin`.**

Changes a project's name, status or Lokalise linkage.

200 the updated project.

**All three body fields are required on every call** — there is no partial-update sentinel here, because `ProjectRepository.Update` takes a full replacement, not a diff. `status` must be `active` or `archived`.

Errors: 403 `forbidden`; 400 `bad_request` (missing name, bad status, unknown JSON field, any query parameter); 404 `not_found` for an unknown project code; 409 `project_code_taken`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token + `is_platform_admin`** — minting a locale administers the project's dimension, it does not translate within it. Locales are admin-managed data now, not migration-seeded reference data.

Adds a locale to a project. Adding one writes **no translation rows** — absent means untranslated — so a seventh locale is cheap by construction, and if it turns out to be a mistake it is reversible by archiving, never by deleting.

201 the created locale (`{"id","project_id","code","flutter_dir","android_values_dir","ios_lproj","sort_order","status"}`), `status` always `active`.

Body rules: `code` required, matching `^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?$`; `flutter_dir`, `android_values_dir` and `ios_lproj` all required and non-empty — these are the export directory names u-mobile's `run.sh` expects; `sort_order` is display order.

Errors: 403 `forbidden`; 400 `bad_request`; 404 `not_found` for an unknown project; 409 `locale_code_taken`; 409 `locale_directory_taken` when another locale on the project already claims one of the three directories — left to the database's UNIQUE constraints rather than pre-checked, because the other locale can appear between a check and the write. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

**Google token + `is_platform_admin`.**

Changes a locale's export directories, sort order or status.

200 the updated locale.

**The locale's `code` cannot be changed by this endpoint at all** — it is the path segment addressing the locale and is deliberately absent from the body, because it is the identifier every translation and history row references and renaming it would silently orphan all of them. `archived` is the only lifecycle move a locale has: there is no delete endpoint, for the same reason. An archived locale stops being servable over OTA (404 `unknown_locale`) rather than freezing on its last bundle forever.

All body fields are written on every call; `status` must be `active` or `archived`.

Errors: 403 `forbidden`; 400 `bad_request` (bad status, empty directory, unknown JSON field, any query parameter); 404 `not_found` for an unknown project or locale code; 409 `locale_directory_taken`. Auth errors on every request in this folder: 401 `missing_token` / `invalid_token` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="u-l10n"`), 403 `not_provisioned` (authenticated by Google but no `users` row), 403 `account_disabled`, 403 `insufficient_role`, 503 `identity_provider_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5` when Google is unreachable, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

item.name: OTA
item.description: Public, unauthenticated, rate-limited. Its own prefix, outside `/api/v1`: the app calls it at launch before login.

header.description: Strict `N.N.N`; anything else is read as 0.0.0.
Send the ETag from the last 200 to get a 304. Disabled by default so the first call returns a full body.

request.description:
**Public — no auth, deliberately.** The app calls this at launch BEFORE login, and the payload is strings that already ship inside the APK/IPA (anyone can unzip them). Requiring auth would add a login dependency to the launch path for no security gain. The real controls are rate limiting, CDN caching, and the by-construction rule that no PII may enter a bundle. **Rate-limited** by the same per-client-IP bucket as `/api/v1`, so a caller cannot multiply its budget across prefixes.

**Request headers**
- `X-App-Version` — validated against `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Anything else (`4.12`, `4.12.0-beta`, `4.12.0 (1234)`) is treated as ABSENT, which the repository reads as `0.0.0` — the conservative floor. That costs an odd client build only the releases that carry a version floor, and never a 500: the header is cast to a Postgres `int[]` in the serving query, and a failed cast would break this unauthenticated hot path.
- `If-None-Match` — full ETag semantics: several values, `*`, and `W/` weak validators are all handled.

**Responses**
- **200** — `{"version","locale","sha256","strings":{...}}` with `ETag: "<sha256>"`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and `Vary: X-App-Version` (without the Vary a CDN could serve a 4.12-only bundle to a 4.09 client).
- **304** — the ETag matched. No body, and the SAME cache headers as the 200, so a CDN knows how long the revalidated entry stays fresh. This is the steady state on every app launch: a few hundred bytes instead of 60-80KB.
- **404 `unknown_locale`** — no such locale for the project, or the locale is archived (from a client's point of view that is what it now is). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`.
- **404 `no_release`** — nothing servable yet. Not an error: the app already has its bundled assets and needs nothing from us. `max-age=60`.
- **410 `release_rolled_back`** — the kill switch. The client must DELETE its cached bundle and fall back to the strings shipped in the app, which a 404 would not signal and a 200-with-empty-body would actively break. `max-age=60`.
- **400 `bad_request`** — any query parameter at all; this route accepts none.
- **429 `rate_limited`** with `Retry-After`.

Both negative answers carry an explicit short TTL so CDN negative caching is a decision rather than a default; a 404 flips to a 200 on the very next publish.

NOTE: this route is not project-prefixed yet — the locale is resolved against project id 1 (YouTrip), marked `TODO(plan-2)` in `route/ota.go`.
